newsitem.title: JAPAN: FORECAST - Japan Dec industry output seen up 0.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Japan Dec industry output seen up 0.7 pct.

text.p: Japan's industrial output is expected to rise by between 0.3 and 1.0 percent in December from a month earlier, economists said.
Economists, on average, predicted a 0.7 percent increase, a notch lower than the 0.8 percent rise forecast by the trade ministry for December's manufacturers' industrial output.
Industrial output data for December will be released by the Ministry of International Trade and Industry at 1.30 p.m. (0430 GMT) on Wednesday.
On the more bearish end, Yasuo Yamamoto of Sanwa Research Institute said he predicted a rise of just 0.3 percent.

Yamamoto said electricity sales had been up 0.5 percent, while export volumes, on a seasonally adjusted month-on-month basis, had fallen 5.0 percent in December. He said he used the Nikkei Economic Electronic Databank System (NEEDS) to obtain month-on-month figures for export volumes.
Other analysts forecast a rise of around one percent, pointing to strong exports of cars to the United States and stepped-up production to meet consumer demand ahead of a sales tax rise in April.

"The production recovery is gaining momentum, inventory adjustment is making rapid progress and looking at customs-cleared trade data for December, the export volume was healthy," said Yasushi Okuda, an economist at BZW Securities.
Others also said that over the past few months that industrial output figures tended to be revised upwards, which had become a factor in their calculations.
